 Pang Ron-Pei Jing refuse to let fatigue, Chinese hurdle derail Finals bid 
Formidable foes: Hoo Pang Ron-Lai Pei Jing face world No. 2 Jiang Zhenbang-Wei Yaxin of China in the second round 
 PETALING JAYA: Hoo Pang Ron-Lai Pei Jing will need to bring out their best when they face world No. 2 Jiang Zhenbang-Wei Yaxin of China in the second round of the Hong Kong Open today.
 There is more than just a quarter-final spot at stake for the Malaysian mixed doubles pair, as a victory would also boost their slim hopes of qualifying for the World Tour Finals in Hangzhou next month.
 Pang Ron-Pei Jing are currently 14th in the World Tour rankings, but they are not giving up hope of making the cut for the season-ending tournament.
 “Of course, we are not putting any big expectations there yet. We are lacking one tournament for Hangzhou.
 “We are just doing our best match by match. Let’s see what the outcome will be at the end,” said Pang Ron in a post-match interview with the Badminton World Federation (BWF).
 However, the Malaysians face a tough challenge against Zhenbang-Yaxin, having lost all three meetings with the Chinese pair this year.
 Their latest defeat came just last week in the second round of the Japan Masters in Kumamoto, where they went down 12-21, 19-21.
 “We will be facing Zhenbang-Yaxin. It’s not an easy match, but we will do our best.
 “We are just trying to fight for ourselves,” said Pei Jing.
 Pang Ron-Pei Jing advanced to the second round after battling past Indonesia’s Marwan Faza-Aisyah Salsabila 21-14, 22-24, 21-13 at the Kai Tak Arena yesterday.
 Fellow Malaysians Goh Soon Huat-Shevon Lai Jemie are also hoping to secure a place in the World Tour Finals despite sitting 15th in the rankings.
 They kept their campaign going with a 21-17, 21-14 win over Americans Chen Zhi Yi-Francesca Corbett and will face another American pair, Presley Smith-Jennie Gai, for a place in the quarter-finals today.
 Only the top eight players or pairs in each event qualify for the World Tour Finals, with the Hong Kong Open offering the final opportunity to collect ranking points before the Dec 9-13 tournament.
